claims.claim: As of Spring '26, new Connected Apps cannot be created; new integrations must use ECAs
claims.quote: As of Spring '26, new Connected Apps cannot be created.
claims.correction: Second page (S3) words it slightly differently: "Connected apps creation is restricted as of Spring '26." and "If you must continue creating connected apps, contact Salesforce Support." So 'cannot' is stated by S1, 'restricted, with a Support route' by S3.

claims.claim: Own-org use is mostly admin configuration; distribution needs packaging, partner enrollment and security review running to several weeks
claims.correction: Characterisation is the author's judgement. The component facts (ISV Partner Program enrollment, packaging, review time frames) are confirmed separately below.

claims.claim: ~3-6 h hands-on estimate
claims.correction: No official page gives an effort figure; it is labelled as an estimate in the guide.

claims.claim: Security review estimates: verification 1-2 weeks, first-time testing 3-4 weeks, resubmission testing 2-3 weeks
claims.quote: Verification: "1-2 weeks." First-time testing: "3-4 weeks." Resubmission: "2-3 weeks." "The time frames are estimates."
claims.correction: Fetch summary gave the figures and the sentence 'The time frames are estimates.' as separate fragments, so the quote above is stitched from fragments, not one sentence. Figures match exactly. Page title now says 'AgentExchange'.

claims.claim: Inside your own org no Salesforce review applies, only admin policy
claims.correction: No official page read states this explicitly. Related fact from S1: Connected Apps created directly in customer orgs are 'out of scope for the May 11 deadline'.

claims.claim: No end-to-end duration is stated
claims.correction: Paraphrase only: the page lists per-stage estimates and no total was seen in the fetched summary. Absence claim, cannot be verbatim-quoted.

claims.claim: Org admin creates ECA via Setup -> App Manager -> New External Client App
claims.quote: From Setup, in the Quick Find box, enter App Manager, and then select App Manager.
claims.correction: The 'New External Client App' button label was not in the extracted text (paraphrase only for that part).

claims.claim: New integrations must use ECA; new Connected Apps cannot be created as of Spring '26
claims.quote: As of Spring '26, new Connected Apps cannot be created.

claims.claim: AppExchange needs ISV Partner Program enrollment, Partner Console connection, scanner results (Code Analyzer, Checkmarx); fee applies, amount not stated
claims.quote: Enroll your solution in the ISV Partner Program. / If you plan to distribute your solution for free, you don't pay the fee.
claims.correction: ISV enrollment, Partner Console (now 'AgentExchange Partner Console'), Code Analyzer and Checkmarx scanner are all confirmed. Fee: the page says a fee is paid through the submission interface but free distribution is exempt, so 'a fee applies' should read 'a fee applies unless you distribute for free'. Amount still not stated. 'Provider profile' was not seen in the fetched text (unsupported).

claims.claim: Create ECA; Distribution State Local or Packaged
claims.quote: To develop an external client app for your local org, select Local. / To develop an external client app for packaging and distribution, set the Distribution State to Packaged.
claims.correction: 'Enter app name and contact email' not separately quoted (paraphrase only).

claims.claim: Enable OAuth Settings, callback URL, scopes
claims.quote: Under API (Enable OAuth Settings), check Enable OAuth Settings.

claims.claim: Mobile SDK guide unchecks Require Secret for Web Server and Refresh Token flows and recommends JWT access tokens (guide marked unverified)
claims.quote: Uncheck Require Secret for Web Server Flow. / Uncheck Require Secret for Refresh Token Flow. / (Recommended) Check Issue JSON Web Token (JWT)-based access tokens for named users.
claims.correction: Can be upgraded from unverified to verified. Quotes are from separate list items. The sentence 'Server-side web apps usually keep the secret requirement' is unsupported by any page read.

claims.claim: Click Create, then Edit; under Policies set Permitted Users to 'Admin approved users are pre-authorized' and pick profiles/permission sets
claims.quote: only users with the associated profile or permission set can access the app without first authorizing it.
claims.correction: Paraphrase only for the exact UI labels and the 'Create then Edit' sequence; the S4 page does not mention Permitted Users. The page title and behaviour match.

claims.claim: Set refresh token expiration and session timeout (DX example uses 90 days and 15 minutes)
claims.quote: Setting a maximum of 90 days for the refresh token expiration is a security best practice. / In the Session Timeout in Minutes box, enter 15.
claims.correction: 90 days is described as a recommended maximum (best practice), not just an example.

claims.claim: ECAs do not support the username-password flow
claims.quote: External client apps don't support username-password flow.
claims.correction: Stated in the migration page's Current Limitations section, not on S4 (the guide cites S4/S6). The generic 'send users to authorization endpoint and exchange the code' text is not directly quoted by any page read.

claims.claim: Partners must meet the four security controls; share only the client key, never the secret
claims.quote: For packaged ECAs, share the client key in the submission documents only — don't share the client secret.
claims.correction: Client-key-only is confirmed. The four controls are scoped: they apply to Connected Apps/ECAs 'included or used in connection with a Partner Application' that are 'in use by more than two customer production orgs' (S1). Single-org and customer-created apps are out of scope. 'Create the ECA in a DevHub/PBO org' was not found in pages read (unsupported).

claims.claim: Mobile SDK allows any URL string; DX example uses http://localhost:1717/OauthRedirect, configurable via oauthLocalPort
claims.quote: Set Callback URL to any URL string, real or fictional, such as mysampleapp://auth/success.
claims.correction: DX page: "in the Callback URL box, enter http://localhost:1717/OauthRedirect" and "update your sfdx-project.json file by setting the oauthLocalPort property to the new port."

claims.claim: General HTTPS or exact-match rules for ECA callback URLs not found
claims.quote: Make sure the callback (redirect) URL in your client exactly matches what is configured in Salesforce.
claims.correction: Exact-match is now supported, but by a hosted-MCP-servers troubleshooting page, not an ECA setup page. No official page read states an HTTPS requirement for ECA callbacks, so that part stays unsupported. Note S4 explicitly allows non-HTTPS custom schemes for mobile.

claims.claim: api, web, refresh_token/offline_access, id/profile/email/address/phone; optional sfap_api and chatbot_api
claims.quote: Access the identity URL service (id, profile, email, address, phone) / Perform requests at any time (refresh_token, offline_access) / (Optional) Access the Salesforce API Platform (sfap_api) / (Optional) Access chatbot services (chatbot_api)
claims.correction: Quotes are from separate list items. api and web also listed ('Manage user data via APIs (api)', '... via Web browsers (web)').

claims.claim: DX page says ECA is ready to use; no dedicated ECA test procedure
claims.quote: Your external client app is ready to use.
claims.correction: 'No test procedure found' is an absence claim.

claims.claim: Permitted Users pre-authorized; Use Any API Client permission still reaches any ECA; policy change can cut off users
claims.quote: If users have the Use Any API Client permission, they can access any external client app.
claims.correction: Lockout: "anyone using the app loses access" when switching from self-authorization to preauthorization, except users whose permissions specifically authorize the app.

claims.claim: AppExchange (AgentExchange) security review required for managed packages and Platform API solutions; in most cases CAs and ECAs must be packaged
claims.quote: CAs and ECAs should be packaged for distribution on AppExchange.
claims.correction: Review requirement confirmed (S8: 'To distribute managed packages, Salesforce Platform API solutions, or Marketing Cloud Engagement API solutions ... they must pass our security review.' - fragments). Packaging: the page says 'should', and says packaging is mandatory for authorization code, client credentials, JWT Bearer and Canvas use cases; otherwise an ECA may be created in the subscriber org after installation and that use case must be documented. 'In most cases must' is imprecise. S8 itself does not mention CAs/ECAs. 'AgentExchange' naming confirmed by S8's title ('How the AgentExchange Security Review Works'); S2 title still says AppExchange.

claims.claim: Review estimates 1-2 / 3-4 / 2-3 weeks
claims.quote: "1-2 weeks", "3-4 weeks", "2-3 weeks"; "The time frames are estimates."
claims.correction: Mapping: verification, first-time testing, resubmission testing respectively. Quote assembled from fragments of the fetch summary.

claims.claim: Four security controls for Connected Apps and ECAs were enforced from May 11, 2026
claims.quote: ISVs have until May 11, 2026 to enforce the security controls
claims.correction: Date confirmed, but it is a partner deadline ('by May 11, 2026'; Salesforce 'will begin enforcing the security requirements as a technical matter' after it), scoped to partner-provided Connected Apps/ECAs used by more than two customer production orgs. Out of scope: single-production-org apps, customer-created apps, Named Credentials S2S. Page says 'there are no plans for a formal extension program'. The four controls are named: OAuth PKCE, Refresh Token Rotation, Refresh Token Idle time-to-live (TTL), Refresh Token IP Allowlist. Whether enforcement actually started on that date is not something the page (a pre-deadline FAQ) can confirm.

claims.claim: Cannot create new Connected App; contact Support if needed; Dev Hub scratch-org case still refers to connected apps; existing keep working and can be migrated if eligible
claims.quote: You can continue to use existing connected apps during and after Spring '26. / If you must continue creating connected apps, contact Salesforce Support.
claims.correction: Spring '26 restriction, Support route and existing-apps-keep-working are confirmed. The Dev Hub scratch-org sentence is unsupported: S3 does not mention Dev Hub or scratch orgs (the DX page title found by search for 'Create a Connected App in Your Org' exists but was not read). Migration of eligible apps is confirmed by the migration page.

claims.claim: Ineligible cases: User Provisioning, custom Apex handlers, Canvas, DCR, SAML Triple DES, SSO apps, some notification subscriptions; migration keeps key/secret; original becomes read-only and should not be deleted
claims.quote: Migration preserves your consumer key and secret, so existing integrations continue to work. / The original connected app is saved as a read-only version. / Don't delete the original connected app after migration.
claims.correction: List is substantively right but imprecise: User Provisioning must be disabled and the Apex handler removed before migrating (fixable); SAML must use AES not Triple DES (fixable); Canvas, DCR and SSO apps cannot be migrated ('You can't migrate single sign-on connected apps to external client apps'); notification case is 'No standard notification subscriptions are configured for non-internal apps'. Also missing: migration cannot detect username-password flow usage. Eligibility is shown by the 'Migrate to External Client App' button in App Manager.

claims.claim: Switching from self-authorization to admin pre-authorization removes access for users not covered
claims.quote: anyone using the app loses access.
claims.correction: The 'assign profiles/permission sets before switching' remedy is the author's advice (paraphrase only).

claims.claim: Missing integration credentials delay review; disclose ECA usage and secret handling; never share the secret
claims.quote: Submit credentials for integrations, including web apps and REST APIs, to avoid delays in the security review.
claims.correction: Also confirmed: "Disclose in detail how Connected Apps and ECAs are used within the solution." and the client-key-only rule.

claims.claim: A failed security review blocks listing until resubmitted with updated scans
claims.quote: You can't list your solution on AgentExchange or distribute it to customers.
claims.correction: Blocking is confirmed; the specific 'updated scans' detail was not seen (paraphrase only). Resubmission testing is a documented stage.

claims.claim: Article 005228017 (new Connected Apps can no longer be created)
claims.correction: JS-rendered shell only ('Salesforce Help'); content does not match title. Guide correctly states nothing relies on it.

claims.claim: Release note: creation of new Connected Apps disabled by default
claims.correction: JS-rendered shell only; content does not match title. Search returned only third-party blogs, not used. The 'disabled by default' wording and any re-enable setting remain unconfirmed.

claims.claim: Exception process / setting to re-enable Connected App creation unknown
claims.quote: If you must continue creating connected apps, contact Salesforce Support.
claims.correction: Partly answerable: a Support-contact route is documented. Whether a self-service setting exists is still unknown (release note unreadable).

claims.claim: Names of the four security controls unknown
claims.quote: OAuth PKCE, Refresh Token Rotation, Refresh Token Idle time-to-live (TTL), and Refresh Token IP Allowlist
claims.correction: Can be removed from unknowns. Exemptions seen: PKCE not required for User Agent flow and no impact on JWT Bearer/Client Credentials; RT IP Allowlist does not apply to end-user device flows or Salesforce-to-Salesforce refresh token flows.

claims.claim: Security review fee amount unknown
claims.quote: If you plan to distribute your solution for free, you don't pay the fee.
claims.correction: Amount still not on the page; fee is paid via the submission interface and waived for free solutions.

claims.claim: Propagation delay for new ECAs or policy changes unknown
claims.correction: No page read mentions propagation delay; remains unknown.

claims.claim: General HTTPS/exact-match rules for ECA callback URLs unknown
claims.quote: Make sure the callback (redirect) URL in your client exactly matches what is configured in Salesforce.
claims.correction: Exact-match now has an official (non-ECA-specific) source; HTTPS rule still not found.

missing: The four required security controls are named (OAuth PKCE, Refresh Token Rotation, Refresh Token Idle TTL, Refresh Token IP Allowlist) with the scope (partner apps used by more than two customer production orgs) and the statement that no formal extension program exists (help.salesforce.com article 005387798).

ECA packaging for AppExchange is mandatory for authorization code, client credentials, JWT Bearer and Canvas use cases; other cases may create the ECA in the subscriber org after install and must document it (article 005232552).

Migration cannot detect username-password flow usage; ECAs do not support that flow, so a migrated app using it stops working. Recommended replacements: OAuth 2.0 web server flow with PKCE, or client credentials flow (migration page, Current Limitations).
